# VariableFunctionsUsage

<Badge type="info" text="info" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="tip" text="quick-fix" />

Group: [Performance](/rules/#performance) · PhpStorm name: `VariableFunctionsUsageInspection`

`call_user_func()` / `forward_static_call()` with a callable that is known at
the call site can be written as a direct call (`$fn(...)`, `Cls::m(...)`,
`$obj->m(...)`), which is faster and analysable. Likewise
`call_user_func_array()` / `forward_static_call_array()` with a literal
argument array can pass the arguments inline.

## Example

Level 8.0+:

::: code-group

```php{7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14} [Before]
<?php
class Mailer {
    public static function send($to, $body) { return true; }
}
$m = new Mailer();

call_user_func($hook, $to, $log);
call_user_func(['Mailer', 'send'], $to, $body);
call_user_func(array($m, 'send'), $to, $body);
forward_static_call([$m, 'send'], ...$rest);
call_user_func([$m, $verb]);
\call_user_func('App\\Mailer::send', $to);
call_user_func_array($hook, [0 => $to, 1 => $body]);
forward_static_call_array('Mailer::send', array(1, 2));

call_user_func_array($hook, []);
call_user_func_array($hook, [&$to]);
call_user_func_array($hook, $args);
call_user_func_array($hook, ['to' => $to, $body]);
call_user_func($hook, $to, &$log);
call_user_func([$pool[0], 'Base::send'], $to);
call_user_func([$m, 'parent::send'], $to);
call_user_func([$pool[0], 'send'], $to);
call_user_func("{$cls}::send", $to);
call_user_func(build(), $to);
$name = 'mailer';
call_user_func([$name, 'send'], $to);
```

```php [After fix]
<?php
class Mailer {
    public static function send($to, $body) { return true; }
}
$m = new Mailer();

$hook($to, $log);
Mailer::send($to, $body);
$m->send($to, $body);
$m::send(...$rest);
$m->$verb();
App\Mailer::send($to);
call_user_func($hook, $to, $body);
forward_static_call('Mailer::send', 1, 2);

call_user_func_array($hook, []);
call_user_func_array($hook, [&$to]);
call_user_func_array($hook, $args);
call_user_func_array($hook, ['to' => $to, $body]);
call_user_func($hook, $to, &$log);
call_user_func([$pool[0], 'Base::send'], $to);
call_user_func([$m, 'parent::send'], $to);
call_user_func([$pool[0], 'send'], $to);
call_user_func("{$cls}::send", $to);
call_user_func(build(), $to);
$name = 'mailer';
call_user_func([$name, 'send'], $to);
```

:::

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 7: Call it directly: &#39;$hook($to, $log)&#39;.</li>
<li>line 8: Call it directly: &#39;Mailer::send($to, $body)&#39;.</li>
<li>line 9: Call it directly: &#39;$m-&gt;send($to, $body)&#39;.</li>
<li>line 10: Call it directly: &#39;$m::send(...$rest)&#39;.</li>
<li>line 11: Call it directly: &#39;$m-&gt;$verb()&#39;.</li>
<li>line 12: Call it directly: &#39;App\Mailer::send($to)&#39;.</li>
<li>line 13: Pass the arguments inline: &#39;call_user_func($hook, $to, $body)&#39;.</li>
<li>line 14: Pass the arguments inline: &#39;forward_static_call(&#39;Mailer::send&#39;, 1, 2)&#39;.</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "VariableFunctionsUsage": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore VariableFunctionsUsage

/**
 * @noinspection VariableFunctionsUsageInspection
 */
```
